newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran expands oil sales to Asia - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iran expands oil sales to Asia - MEES.

text.p: Iran is diverting more of its crude exports under term contracts into lucrative Asian markets, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

"Lifting data for the first eight months of 1996 sugggest that Iran has been directing a growing share of its export slate into the generally more profitable East of Suez marketplace," the Cyprus-based weekly said.

Asian customers lifted nearly one million barrels per day (bpd) of Iranian oil between January and August, compared to just under 800,000 bpd in 1995, according to a MEES analysis on Iranian export schedules this year.
Iran's crude exports average between 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) and 2.6 million bpd, making Iran the world's third largest crude exporter behind Saudi Arabia and Norway.
Europe is the largest market for Iranian crude.
Tehran lost its American oil customers last year following a decree from U.S. President Bill Clinton banning crude purchases by U.S. firms.
U.S. firms lifted up a quarter of Iran's total export slate before the ban.
The upturn in Iran's Asian marketing was led by higher sales to Japan, South Korea, China, Thailand and India and helped by term contract prices below those of spot Iranian crude barrels.

"While National Iranian Oil Company has been selling spot cargos at premiums of as much as 15-20 cents a barrel over the official Asian formulas recently, those companies which agree to increase contractural volumes under annual term arrangemnets are guaranteed the incremental supplies at no extra cost," MEES reported.
